subject: general
question: _________ is the sanctum sanctorum, the innermost sanctuary of Hindu and Jain temples where resides the murti (idol) of the primary deity of the temple.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Garbhagriha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A garbhagriha or sannidhanam is the sanctum sanctorum, the innermost sanctuary of a Hindu and Jain temples **where resides the murti of the primary deity of the temple.
 
• Literally the **word means "womb chamber"**, from the Sanskrit words garbha for womb and griha for the house.
 
• Although the term is often associated with Hindu temples, it is also found in Jain and Buddhist temples.
 
• Traditionally, in Hinduism only 'priests' are allowed to enter this chamber, though in modern practice this is often considerably relaxed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Vimana is the structure over the garbhagriha or inner sanctum in the** Hindu temples of South India **and **Odisha in East India**. 
 
• Shikhara, a Sanskrit word translating literally to "**mountain peak**", refers to the rising tower in the Hindu temple architecture of North India, and also often used in **Jain temples**.
 
• Mandapa in Indian architecture, **especially Hindu temple architecture**, is a pillared hall or pavilion for public rituals.
 
• Mandapas are described as **open or closed** depending on whether they have walls.
 
• In temples, one or more mandapas very often lie between the sanctuary and the temple entrance, on the same axis.
